subject: Renewal: Premium SLA + Burst trial / Proof-of-performance
messages:
From: Tom Silva <tom.silva@aurorapay.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aurorapay.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — premium SLA ask + PoP request

Hi Jonas,

We’re coming up on our renewal and are evaluating a move to Redwood’s Premium SLA. Two asks from our side: a) guarantee tighter latency SLOs for the API (95th percentile under 120ms at our committed baseline, with tail mitigations for spikes) and b) a short proof-of-performance (PoP) — two-week pilot to validate burst behavior and tail latency under real traffic.

If Redwood can run a PoP and provide a simple retainer/credit structure that offsets the incremental premium, we’ll prioritize the upsell in procurement. Please include cadence for measurement, what telemetry you’ll provide, and any minimum committed throughput required.

We’ll also need SOC2 evidence for procurement and an outline of how rollback/fallback will work during the PoP.

Thanks,
Tom Silva
Head of Platform, AuroraPay
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Attachment: sample-traffic-profile.json (stub)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Tom Silva <tom.silva@aurorapay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — premium SLA ask + PoP request

Tom — thanks for the clear asks, this is doable and I’ve sketched a practical path below. High level: 2-week PoP + 3‑month committed term extension to lock in baseline throughput and discounted premium retainer for the ramp. Key points we propose: 

- PoP scope: two weeks in your dev/staging linked environment using production-like samples. We’ll instrument 95th/99th latencies, KV cache hit rates, and model variant fallbacks.
- SLO target for Premium (proposal): 95th <= 120ms, p99 action threshold and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if p99 breaches for > 60s.
- Capacity: commit to baseline throughput of 20 requests/sec with burst allowance up to 100 requests/sec for the PoP window.
- Billing model: provide a one-time onboarding credit to offset PoP ops + 25% discount on the premium retainer for the first 3 months if you commit to a 12-month extension after PoP.

I’ve attached a draft SOW and a short PoP test plan — please review. Marissa and Ben are looped for pricing and contract mechanics. If this looks okay, we’ll send a mutual action plan and DocuSign for the term amendment.

Next steps:
1) You confirm the sample traffic window and PoP start date (we can target week of Apr 20).
2) Procurement: which SOC2 artifacts do you need (summary vs full report)? We can provide SOC2 summary and audit contact.
3) Marissa will follow up on the exact retainer numbers and DocuSign link.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0222

Attachments: Aurora_Renewal_SOW_v1.pdf; Proof_of_Performance_TestPlan.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Silva <tom.silva@aurorapay.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — premium SLA ask + PoP request

Tom — quick note from pricing. Per Jonas’s outline, we can do the following package: 

- PoP: no charge for the two-week test (we’ll credit standard retainer equivalent to onboarding hours).
- If AuroraPay signs a 12-month term extension within 30 days of PoP completion, we’ll apply: 20% discount on the monthly premium retainer for months 1–6 and a one-time operational credit of $15k to offset migration/testing costs.
- Standard price for Premium SLA after discounts will be outlined in the DocuSign amendment.

Procurement asks we commonly get: SOC2 summary (PDF), an ops runbook excerpt, and the SSO/KMS integration checklist. We’ll attach the SOC2 summary and the runbook excerpt when I send the amendment.

Please confirm the PoP start date window — I’ll prepare the amendment and have legal ready for a quick signature once you accept.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0088
From: Tom Silva <tom.silva@aurorapay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aurorapay.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — premium SLA ask + PoP request

All — appreciate the fast turnaround. We accept the proposed PoP and the credit/discount structure subject to procurement sign-off. Proposed PoP kickoff: Tuesday Apr 20 at 09:00 PT. Procurement wants the SOC2 summary and a contact for the security lead for a short Q&A. I’ve attached procurement’s checklist; please confirm you can meet those items.

One more ask: during PoP we’ll want a simple SLA dashboard feed (a short JSON/CSV daily summary) showing 95th, p99, error rates, and KV cache hit rate. Can you confirm format?

Thanks,
Tom

Attachment: aurorapay_procurement_checklist.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Tom — great, we’ll proceed with Apr 20 kickoff. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- SOC2: sending SOC2_Summary_2026.pdf and intro to our security lead (security@redwood.ai) in a separate thread for the Q&A.
- Dashboard feed: we’ll provide a daily CSV feed (S3 signed URL) and a lightweight JSON webhook with the fields you requested (timestamp, p50, p95, p99, error_rate, kv_cache_hit). We’ll include a sample CSV in the PoP kit.
- Mutual Action Plan: attached — outlines dates, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria. Please review the acceptance criteria section (p95 <= 120ms for 10 out of 14 PoP days, and no sustained p99 breach > 60s).
- DocuSign: Marissa will send the amendment link; once signed and PoP signs off we’ll finalize a 12-month term amendment and apply credits.

Thanks — see you on Apr 20.

Jonas Weber
